title: Certified bounds for the Mertens function: lim sup M(x)/sqrt(x) > 2.06175 and lim inf M(x)/sqrt(x) < -2.06471
description:
A self-contained, independently checkable proof that lim sup M(x)/√x > 2.0617536514585282 and lim inf M(x)/√x < −2.0647155435291726, where M(x) is the Mertens function. This improves the best previously published bounds, 1.826054 and −1.837625 (G. Hurst, Math. Comp. 2018), on both sides, and supersedes version 1.0.0 of this record (1.9203693129093421 / −1.9205369736317600). Since both bounds exceed 2, |M(x)| ≤ 2√x fails for arbitrarily large x, which answers the question raised by J. Pintz (arXiv:2608.24878, §2).

The proof applies Ingham's theorem (in the form of Odlyzko and te Riele 1985 and Hurst 2018) at two explicit points, evaluating the required finite sum over the first 14 400 zeros of the Riemann zeta function in ball arithmetic. The package contains the statement and proof, the two points, the zero data with rigorous radii, two verifiers based on different libraries (FLINT/Arb and mpmath interval arithmetic), a zero-data regenerator and a validation guide. The search procedure that found the points is not included and is not needed for verification.

Nearly all of the code, computations and documentation were produced by an AI system (Claude, by Anthropic) under the direction of Benjamin Weisz, who is responsible for the content. The work has not been peer reviewed. Data and documentation are licensed CC BY 4.0; code is licensed Apache-2.0.
